name: PCA9555PW,118
title: PCA9555: 16-bit I2C-bus and SMBus I/O expander with interrupt output
summary: A CMOS port expander that gives an I2C-bus or SMBus master sixteen general-purpose I/O lines, arranged as two 8-bit ports. Each line is set as input or output on its own, inputs can be read inverted, and an open-drain active-LOW INT output flags any input change. It runs from 2.3 to 5.5 V, its I/Os tolerate 5 V, it clocks at up to 400 kHz, and three address pins put up to eight on one bus. All I/Os come up as inputs with weak pull-ups.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A 5 V master controller drives the PCA9555 over SCL and SDA and takes its INT line; each of the three lines has a 10 kΩ pull-up to VDD. A0, A1 and A2 are all grounded, giving slave address 0100 000x. Port 0 serves several jobs: IO0_0 sinks current for an LED fed through 2 kΩ from VDD, IO0_2 drives the active-LOW RESET of a counter, IO0_3 drives the ENABLE of a bus switch joining A and B, while IO0_1 reads a temperature sensor's INT, IO0_4 reads an alarm system's ALARM and IO0_5 reads a push-button returned to VDD through a resistor. IO0_6, IO0_7 and all of port 1 read a ten-digit keypad.
notes: IO0_0, IO0_2 and IO0_3 are set as outputs; every other I/O is set as an input.
The keypad's pins are numbered 1 to 10 in the order of the I/Os they reach, IO0_6 first.

circuits.title: Test circuitry for switching times
circuits.description: A pulse generator, terminated by RT to ground, drives the input of the device under test (VI). The output (VO) carries CL = 50 pF to ground and RL = 500 Ω to a switch that ties RL to VDD, to GND or leaves it open. RT matches the generator's output impedance Zo; CL counts the jig and probe capacitance.

equations.note: Eight address settings let eight devices share one bus.

operation.text: Sixteen I/O lines in two 8-bit ports, each line chosen as input or output on its own. Each port has four 8-bit registers: Input, Output, Polarity Inversion and Configuration. The I2C-bus address matches the PCF8575 and the pinout is the same, but its added features mean software written for the PCF8575 has to change. The fixed address part is the same as the PCA9554's, so up to eight of either kind, mixed, can share a bus.
After the address byte of a write, the next byte selects one of the eight registers (0 to 7); later reads and writes start from that register.
Read-only. They show the logic level on every pin, output or input. Writing to them does nothing.
Hold the levels driven on pins set as outputs; a bit has no effect on a pin set as input. Reading them returns the flip-flop contents, not the pin level. Default 1.
A 1 in a bit flips the sense of that pin's bit in the Input port register; a 0 leaves it as is. Default 0.
A 1 makes the pin an input with its output driver off; a 0 makes it an output. Each pin carries a high-value resistor (100 kΩ) to VDD. After reset every pin is an input pulled up to VDD.

An internal reset holds the device until VDD rises to VPOR; then all registers and the SMBus state machine take their defaults. To reset by cycling the supply, VDD has to fall below 0.2 V, for at least 5 µs.

As an input, both output transistors (Q1 to VDD, Q2 to VSS) are off and the pin is high impedance, weakly pulled to VDD; an input may be driven above VDD up to 5.5 V. As an output, one of Q1 or Q2 conducts according to the Output port bit, so an external voltage forced onto an output meets a low-impedance path to VDD or VSS.

The master sends the address with R/W = 0, then the command byte, then data. The registers work as four pairs (Input, Output, Polarity Inversion, Configuration); after each data byte the pointer moves to the other register of the pair, so writing register 3 then stores the next byte in register 2. Any number of data bytes may follow in one transfer. Output data appears on the port within tv(Q) after the acknowledge.

The master writes the address and command byte, sends a repeated START, then the address with R/W = 1. The device returns the chosen register, then its pair partner, alternating for as many bytes as the master acknowledges; the master leaves the last byte unacknowledged before STOP. Input data is captured as the acknowledge clock pulse falls. A STOP can end the transfer at any point.

INT, open drain, goes LOW when a pin set as input changes state. It is released when that input goes back to its earlier level or when the Input port register holding it is read. Pins set as outputs never raise it. Ports 0 and 1 are read separately, so reading one port does not clear an interrupt from the other. Switching a pin from output to input can give a false interrupt when the pin level differs from the Input port register contents.
SCL and SDA have a noise filter (spikes up to tSP = 50 ns are suppressed). The device runs from 0 Hz to 400 kHz clock, and the I/Os do not glitch on power-up.

SDA and SCL each need a pull-up to a positive supply. Data on SDA changes only while SCL is LOW; SDA falling while SCL is HIGH is a START, SDA rising while SCL is HIGH is a STOP. Every byte is followed by an acknowledge bit, the receiver pulling SDA LOW during the ninth clock; a master reading ends by not acknowledging the last byte.
External limits: 25 mA per I/O, 100 mA per 8-bit port and 200 mA for the device; the current sourced by all I/Os together is 160 mA at most.
ESD protection beyond 2000 V HBM (JESD22-A114), 200 V MM (JESD22-A115) and 1000 V CDM (JESD22-C101). Latch-up tested to JESD78, beyond 100 mA. Handle with ESD precautions per JESD625-A.

SMD packages: lead-free reflow peaks follow the lead-free table (245 to 260 °C by thickness and volume), SnPb peaks the SnPb table; small packages run hotter in reflow; observe the moisture sensitivity level on the packing. Leaded SMDs with pitch under about 0.6 mm, ball-grid parts, and some no-lead parts whose lands sit beneath the body, are unsuited to wave soldering. DIP: wave dwell typically 3 to 4 s at 250 °C (SnPb) or 265 °C (Pb-free), total wave contact no more than 5 s, body never above Tstg(max). Hand soldering: iron of 24 V or less, applied below the seating plane or within 2 mm above it, up to 10 s below 300 °C bit temperature or up to 5 s from 300 to 400 °C.
